chain.label: No FAA direct surveillance of Hawaii air tour operations
chain.trigger: At the time of the Heli-USA accident, the Honolulu FSDO still did not have a means to provide direct surveillance of air tour activities.

chain.label: No reliable weather observation coverage for Kauai north shore
chain.trigger: No weather reporting facility is located on the north end of the island where the accident occurred, and the weather facility on the south end of the island is unable to observe the weather on the north end reliably because of interference from high terrain

chain.label: Helicopter had no flotation equipment; SFAR 71 did not require it
chain.trigger: The helicopter was not equipped, and was not required to be equipped, with flotation equipment.

chain.label: Loose/improperly seated PFD inflation cylinders
chain.trigger: Examination revealed that the threaded cylinder for that chamber was not screwed securely into its housing... the operator reported that 18 of the 26 cylinders were loose in their housings.

chain.label: Rapidly developing convective cells with heavy rain and microburst potential over the accident area
chain.trigger: satellite infrared imagery ... indicated the rapid development of cumulus clouds capable of producing heavy rain showers, and stability and energy indices indicated potentially strong updrafts and downdrafts ... supported the presence of embedded wet-type microburst activity

chain.label: Pilot continued the tour into a visible heavy rain shower rather than turning back
chain.trigger: The pilot stated that he saw rain showers offshore as the flight approached Kee Beach and Kailiu Point... Both of these passengers said that their helicopter made no evasive maneuver, or any maneuver, before entering what they described as 'a wall of pure rain and thick clouds.'

caused_by.evidence: of the three other tour pilots who approached the storm associated with the accident, one elected to turn back without entering the conditions and two chose to fly through it

In the absence of reliable and timely official weather information, Kauai air tour pilots typically use their own judgment on the basis of the appearance of the weather to determine whether to proceed.

chain.label: Helicopter entered heavy rain and localized IMC with sharply reduced visibility
chain.trigger: when he leveled his helicopter out of the turn, it was 'already inside the storm,' and it encountered heavy rain

caused_by.evidence: the helicopter made no evasive maneuvers before entering the adverse weather
Localized instrument meteorological conditions (IMC) prevailed in the vicinity of the accident site.

chain.label: Pilot slowed and descended below SFAR 71 minimum altitude instead of terminating the tour
chain.trigger: he reduced the helicopter's airspeed and initiated a descent to maintain visual reference to the beach

caused_by.evidence: while the helicopter was in the heavy rain, he could still see down and to the right to the coastline
there is evidence that pilots from multiple operators were not properly following these procedures and that there was little threat of enforcement consequences for doing so

chain.label: Helicopter operating low over the shoreline with little altitude margin
chain.trigger: Of the three pilots who chose to enter the adverse weather, all had to descend below the SFAR 71 minimum altitude to maintain visual contact with the shore.

caused_by.evidence: he started a right turn over the beach

chain.label: Encounter with wet microburst downdraft during course reversal
chain.trigger: Statements from the pilot and passengers regarding the helicopter's rapid descent in torrential rain are consistent with an encounter with a microburst event.

caused_by.evidence: the sounding was favorable for microburst development with outflow winds of 55 knots

chain.label: Airspeed decayed to zero and helicopter descended rapidly despite full power
chain.trigger: during the turn, the helicopter's airspeed dropped to zero and the helicopter started to rapidly descend... The pilot added full power and control inputs, but the helicopter continued to descend

caused_by.evidence: microbursts ... cause both vertical and horizontal windshears that can be extremely hazardous to all types and categories of aircraft, especially at altitudes below 1,000 feet
the conditions can produce a situation in which it is difficult to control the aircraft

chain.label: Control inputs ineffective; helicopter entered a hard left spin over the water
chain.trigger: his control inputs were not effective... the helicopter went back up in the air momentarily and entered an immediate hard spin to the left, which took the flight over the water

caused_by.evidence: he realized that the helicopter was going to hit the beach at a high rate of descent

chain.label: Helicopter struck the ocean, rolled right, and sank quickly
chain.trigger: the helicopter hit the water, bounced back into the air, and continued to spin... then it rolled to the right and immediately began to sink

caused_by.evidence: it crashed into the water several hundred feet off shore

helicopter floats would have likely kept the helicopter on the water surface longer... all of the passengers would have had the opportunity to don their PFDs and egress the helicopter successfully had the helicopter not sunk so quickly

chain.label: Three passengers drowned; pilot and two passengers received minor injuries
chain.trigger: Three passengers were killed, and the commercial pilot and two other passengers received minor injuries... the cause of death for the passengers ... was 'drowning'

caused_by.evidence: The helicopter sank quickly; thus, the passengers had little time to help themselves or others before they were submerged.
The other recovered PFD with one uninflated chamber showed evidence that someone had attempted to inflate it but was unsuccessful, likely because of an incompletely seated cylinder.
